title: Finding the stepfather work and sending them to Chicago
summary: The new stepfather could find no job, Gus got jobs for both, then sent them to Des Moines and Chicago where he made hydraulic jacks.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So they're there now.

He said, 'Well, I'm going to try to find a job here.' I said, 'You can't find no job here unless I give it to you,' just like that. He said, 'Oh, I'll find something.' I said, 'Okay, you find it.' He couldn't find nothing.
Because you guys had it all sewed up.
We had it all sewed up. I just don't
believe that. I'm telling you this but that I don't believe it. He couldn't find anything.
So what did you do?

Yeah, I got him a job. And my mother wanted a job, so I said, 'Oh, you don't need to work,' one of those things. She wanted a job, so, okay, I got her a job out there at the club where I was playing. And she was cooking there at the club, see. And that's the way it was.
And so he couldn't find anything he really wanted, nothing. He couldn't find nothing. So he said, 'Well, would you take me to Des Moines?' I said, 'What are you going to do there?'
You were salty with him, really.
Yeah, I was. I was really salty about it, but he turned out to be a A-1 guy. He's always been in my corner.
Fancy that.
Yeah, he took sick while he was in Ottumwa, and so I got a doctor for him, one of those things. But he's always been in my corner, always.
Did they stay married?
They're still together, sure.
Oh, now, that is a funny one, isn't it? So it wasn't a fly-by-night thing at all.
No, no. That's what I figured, though.
But it was hard on him, though, wasn't it?
Yeah, but --
Well, the fact that you didn't know anything about it.
No, I didn't know anything about it and I didn't know what was what.
Yeah.
I thought it was just one of them things, put on to me.
Isn't that funny?
But it wasn't.
That's very funny, isn't it?

I carried him to Des Moines and he got a job there. They stayed there for a little while. He told me he'd like to go to Chicago where his brother is. And I said, "What are you going to do there?" And he said, "Maybe I can get a job there, the kind I'd like."
So I sent both of them to Chicago, and he got there and got him a good job there.
What did he get?
He started working for Walker's, hydraulic jacks, you know?
Oh, oh.
Oh, he can just really make a jack, he
can put a jack together.
Oh.
He learned all that from --
He was a guy that was ready to work.
Oh, yeah, that's right. That's the way he's always been.
And so they settled there.
They settled there. They stayed there for years, until they came to New York to live with me, in New York. And they've been out here to live, too.
Is that right? That's good, that's nice.
Yeah.
